walkthrough.setup.title: Get Started with Secondary Simulator
walkthrough.setup.description: Put the device preview beside your code, then connect a simulator.
walkthrough.setup.move.title: Move the preview to the Secondary Side Bar
walkthrough.setup.move.description:
The preview starts in the Activity Bar, where it covers the file tree. Moving it to the Secondary Side Bar puts the device beside your code instead.
1. Right-click the Secondary Simulator icon (the phone) in the Activity Bar
2. Choose Move To
3. Choose Secondary Side Bar

Dragging the icon to the right edge of the window does the same thing. To undo it, right-click the icon again and pick Move To → Side Bar.
walkthrough.setup.move.altText: Right-clicking the Secondary Simulator icon in the Activity Bar, then Move To, then Secondary Side Bar
walkthrough.setup.connect.title: Connect a device
walkthrough.setup.connect.description:
Boot an iOS Simulator or Android Emulator and it is picked up automatically. To choose one yourself, or to boot a stopped device, use the device list.
[Select Device](command:simulator.selectDevice)
macOS with Xcode is required for the iOS Simulator; Android needs the Android SDK and adb.
configuration.autoConnect.description: Connect automatically to a running device. While disconnected, looks for devices every 5 seconds and attaches to newly booted simulators too. Kept in sync with the Auto button in the sidebar; pressing Disconnect turns it off.
configuration.directStream.description: Send frames straight to the webview instead of through the extension host, so Chromium decodes them natively. With sidecar capture on the iOS Simulator the sidecar serves them on 127.0.0.1; otherwise the mobilecli MJPEG stream is relayed. Experimental.
configuration.streamScale.description: iOS: MJPEG scaling factor (1.0 = original size). Lower values reduce bandwidth (sets WDA's mjpegScalingFactor).
configuration.streamQuality.description: iOS: MJPEG JPEG quality (1-100). Use together with streamScale to tune bandwidth.
configuration.keyInput.description: iOS: how keyboard input is delivered. Touch always stays on HID. Choose wda when you want the software keyboard visible in the sidebar.
configuration.keyInput.enum.hid: Direct HID injection (fast). The simulator treats it as a hardware keyboard, so the software keyboard stays hidden.
configuration.keyInput.enum.wda: Through WDA (about 370ms per character). The software keyboard stays visible and the device's input source (Latin/Kana) does not interfere.
configuration.captureSource.description: iOS: where the screen is captured from. auto reads the framebuffer directly when the HID sidecar is available and falls back to WDA otherwise.
configuration.captureSource.enum.auto: Capture the device framebuffer directly when the HID sidecar is available on the iOS Simulator. The software keyboard and status bar are included.
configuration.captureSource.enum.wda: Use the mobilecli/WDA MJPEG stream as before. WDA screenshots only draw the application window, so the software keyboard is not captured.
configuration.captureFps.description: iOS: idle capture rate for the sidecar, in fps. Frames are not sent while the screen is unchanged. While you are touching the screen the rate rises automatically, up to twice this value and no more than 60fps.
configuration.captureMaxWidth.descriptio: iOS: upper bound for the width (px) of JPEG frames from the sidecar. The actual width follows the sidebar's display width (times devicePixelRatio) and is capped here. Raising it looks sharper and costs more bandwidth.
configuration.captureMode.description: iOS: how sidecar capture is driven.
configuration.captureMode.enum.auto: Use display change notifications when available, capturing the moment the screen changes and removing the 16.7ms average delay that polling adds. Falls back to polling automatically when they are unavailable or stop arriving.
configuration.captureMode.enum.poll: Always capture by polling. Change notifications rely on a private API, so pin this when an Xcode update breaks them.
configuration.logLevel.description: How much detail is written to the "Secondary Simulator" output channel. VS Code keeps the whole channel in memory with no way to drop old lines, so keep this at info or lower for everyday use.
configuration.logLevel.enum.debug: Verbose, including received messages. Use only while investigating.
command.record.title: Record Screen
configuration.showDeviceFrame.descriptio: Draw the phone bezel around the screen. Turn it off to use the full width of a narrow sidebar.
configuration.showResourceStats.descript: Show memory and extension-size figures in the footer. These are developer diagnostics; the video rate and input path are always shown.
configuration.showTouchesInRecording.des: Turn on Android’s "Show taps" while recording, so the video shows where the screen was touched. The ripples drawn in the sidebar are not part of the recording — Android records on the device itself. The previous value is restored when the recording stops; if the editor is killed mid-recording, the setting stays on until the next recording. Android only.
configuration.saveLocation.description: Initial folder for the screenshot and screen-recording save dialogs.
configuration.saveLocation.enum.workspac: The first workspace folder. Falls back to the home directory when no folder is open.
configuration.saveDirectory.description: Custom folder path when saveLocation is custom. Ignored otherwise.
